raw_case_text:
The case is a 32-year-old female patient with a history of cadaveric donor RT in 2006 due to membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis. She received induction therapy with basiliximab and maintenance therapy with tacrolimus, mycophenolate, and deflazacort. She consulted for a 4-week history of diarrheal stools 4 times a day that she controlled with loperamide. In the last week, it was associated with nausea, crampy abdominal pain, and fever. In the last 6 months, she had lost 10 kg and was being managed with oral iron due to normochromic normocytic anemia, with no improvement in hemoglobin levels. She had no other relevant background.
On physical examination, she was tachycardic, afebrile, and normotensive, with abdominal pain in the left flank without signs of peritoneal irritation. Chronic diarrhea and febrile syndrome were considered in an immunosuppressed patient, so studies with fecal microscopy, fecal culture, viral load for CMV, and blood culture were started (Table 1). Due to chronic anemia, studies with folic acid, vitamin B12, ferrokinetic profile, and nutritional profile were extended, confirming iron deficiency anemia.
Renal function was stable with serum creatinine within the patient's usual range. Electrolytes were unaltered, fecal microscopy examination was inflammatory, and cultures were negative. Colonoscopy showed left and transverse colitis with 80% stenosis of the colonic lumen (Figure 1). Biopsies of the compromised segments were taken.
Given the results found in colonoscopy, studies with gastrointestinal film array, CMV viral load in plasma, HIV, and rapid plasma reagin were evaluated, which were negative, as was the Histoplasma urine antigen. Herpes simplex type I and II studies performed in biopsy were negative. Given the suspicion of neoplasia, contrast abdominal tomography was carried out, which showed thickening and enhancement of the walls of the cecum, ascending colon, and hepatic flexure of the colon, with a 4-cm segment with 80% stenosis of the ascending colon lumen. Colon biopsy reported ulcerative component, without identifying microorganisms, dysplasia, or malignancy. Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for TB and CMV was positive in the biopsy.
The patient was presented at a meeting considering intestinal Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MT) and CMV coinfection. Treatment with valganciclovir for 4 weeks was decided to manage CMV and 4-drug therapy with isoniazid (INH), rifampin (R), pyrazinamide (Z), ethambutol (E), and pyridoxine for GITB management. Tacrolimus dose was adjusted due to drug interaction with rifampin.
During treatment, elevated transaminases (aspartate aminotransferase 414 U/L and alanine transaminase 990 U/L) and uric acid (16 mg/dL) developed. Hepatotoxicity associated with INH was considered, so it was assessed by the pulmonologist who changed INH to moxifloxacin, with improvement in the liver profile. Moxifloxacin, R, and Z were continued for 9 months. The evolution was satisfactory, with the resolution of diarrhea, improvement in anemia, stable renal function (1.48 mg/dL), and weight recovery.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 32-year-old female long-term renal transplant recipient presented with a 4-week history of watery diarrhea (4 episodes daily) accompanied during the final week by nausea, crampy left flank pain, and fever, superimposed on a 6-month history of a 10 kg weight loss and oral-iron-refractory anemia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Having undergone deceased-donor renal transplantation in 2006 for membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis and maintained on tacrolimus, mycophenolate, and deflazacort, the patient developed 6 months of progressive 10 kg weight loss and iron-deficiency anemia unresponsive to oral iron, followed by 4 weeks of non-bloody watery diarrhea and 1 week of fever, nausea, and crampy left flank pain. Abdominal CT and colonoscopy revealed diffuse left, transverse, and ascending colitis with a 4-cm stenotic (80% luminal narrowing) mass-like lesion in the ascending colon initially suspected to be colon malignancy.
subjective.past_medical_history: End-stage renal disease secondary to membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis status post deceased-donor renal transplantation in 2006 (basiliximab induction; maintenance immunosuppression with tacrolimus, mycophenolate, and deflazacort) and a 6-month history of iron-deficiency anemia.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for chronic watery diarrhea, fever, nausea, crampy left flank pain, 10 kg weight loss, and fatigue. Home medications included tacrolimus, mycophenolate, deflazacort, and oral iron.

objective.physical_examination: Tachycardic, afebrile, and normotensive at examination; abdominal palpation revealed tenderness in the left flank without peritoneal signs.
objective.routine_investigations: Baseline labs confirmed iron-deficiency anemia with stable allograft function (serum creatinine 1.48 mg/dL at follow-up) and normal serum electrolytes. Stool microscopy showed an inflammatory pattern, while stool bacterial cultures, blood cultures, stool multiplex PCR (GI FilmArray), HIV serology, RPR, and urinary Histoplasma antigen were all negative. During subsequent anti-tuberculous therapy, she developed transient isoniazid-induced hepatotoxicity (AST 414 U/L, ALT 990 U/L) and pyrazinamide-related hyperuricemia (uric acid 16 mg/dL).
objective.advanced_workup: Quantitative plasma cytomegalovirus (CMV) viral load was negative. Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT demonstrated circumferential wall thickening and mucosal hyperenhancement involving the cecum, ascending colon, and hepatic flexure with a 4-cm segment of 80% luminal stenosis in the ascending colon. Colonoscopy showed ulcerative colitis involving the left and transverse colon and a stenotic ascending colon lesion narrowing the lumen by 80%; colonic mucosal biopsies showed active ulcerative inflammation negative for dysplasia, malignancy, and HSV-1/2, while tissue PCR performed directly on the colonic biopsy specimen was simultaneously positive for both Mycobacterium tuberculosis and cytomegalovirus (CMV).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Synchronous stenosing intestinal Mycobacterium tuberculosis (gastrointestinal tuberculosis) and cytomegalovirus (CMV) ulcerative colitis co-infection mimicking ascending colon carcinoma in a long-term renal transplant recipient, confirmed by concurrent positive colonic biopsy tissue PCR for both M. tuberculosis and CMV despite an undetectable plasma CMV viral load. Treated with a 4-week course of oral valganciclovir alongside quadruple anti-tuberculous therapy (isoniazid, rifampin [with tacrolimus dose adjustment], pyrazinamide, ethambutol, and pyridoxine; isoniazid was substituted with moxifloxacin due to transaminitis, completing 9 months of moxifloxacin, rifampin, and pyrazinamide), resulting in complete resolution of diarrhea, normalization of hemoglobin, weight restoration, and preserved renal allograft function (creatinine 1.48 mg/dL).
